- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- Model underperforms when sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 3–5 day lagged sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle reversal; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for days 25–30 if sentiment drops below 0.50.
- If sentiment is uniformly high across 18-day window, model tends to overfit recent trend; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast to reduce noise.
